in_arabic.name: حرام
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحرام هو كل ما حرمه الله تعالى في القرآن الكريم أو السنة النبوية، ويشمل الأفعال والأشياء التي تعتبر محرمة أو ممنوعة في الإسلام، مثل أكل لحم الخنزير أو شرب الخمر.

in_urdu.name: حرام
in_urdu.meaning: اسلام میں ممنوع یا حرام چیز
in_urdu.long_meaning: حرام وہ چیز ہے جو اللہ تعالیٰ نے قرآن کریم یا سنت نبوی میں حرام کی ہے، اور اس میں ایسے کام اور چیزیں شامل ہیں جو اسلامی قانون کے مطابق ممنوع ہیں، جیسے کہ سور کا گوشت کھانا یا شراب پینا۔

in_hindi.name: हराम
in_hindi.meaning: इस्लाम में निषिद्ध या हराम चीज़
in_hindi.long_meaning: हराम वह चीज़ है जो अल्लाह तआला ने कुरआन करीम या सुन्नत नबवी में निषिद्ध की है, और इसमें वे कार्य और चीज़ें शामिल हैं जो इस्लामी कानून के अनुसार निषिद्ध हैं, जैसे कि सूअर का मांस खाना या शराब पीना।

in_pashto.name: حرام
in_pashto.meaning: په اسلام کې منع یا حرام شی
in_pashto.long_meaning: حرام هغه شی دی چې الله تعالی په قرآن کریم یا سنت نبوي کې یې منع کړی دی، او پدې کې هغه کړنې او شیان شامل دي چې د اسلامي قانون له مخې منع دي، لکه د خنزیر غوښ خوړل یا د شرابو څښل.

in_english.name: Haraam
in_english.long_meaning: Haraam refers to actions or things that are strictly prohibited in Islam, as stated in the Quran or the Hadith. The term encompasses a range of forbidden acts and objects, including dietary restrictions and moral codes. The concept of Haraam is fundamental to Islamic jurisprudence and guides Muslims in their daily lives.

data.cultural_impact: The concept of Haram is deeply embedded in Islamic culture, governing various aspects of Muslim daily life. It extends from Dietary laws such as the prohibition of pork and alcohol, to moral and ethical rules, like the avoidance of adultery, theft and lying. The term serves as a reminder for Muslims to maintain a strong moral compass, keep their actions and habits in check, and adhere to their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the label of Haram acts as a deterrent from indulging in unlawful activities, and a guide towards conformity with Allah's commands. It also underscores the importance of self-control, discipline, and self-reflection, which are all integral parts of Islamic spirituality. By abstaining from Haram actions, Muslims strengthen their bond with Allah, serving as a testament to their devotion and submission.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hazm's 'The Ring of the Dove' (10th century AD), describes haraam as anything forbidden by Allah or the Prophet Muhammad.
The Islamic term 'haraam' was also used to refer to areas in Arabia that were considered sacred and off-limits to non-Muslims during the early Islamic period (7th-9th centuries AD).
